definition: Infer.NET is a free and open source .NET software library for machine learning.
details: It supports running Bayesian inference in graphical models and can also be used for probabilistic programming.

explainer.lead: Infer.NET is a free, open-source .NET library for machine learning that runs Bayesian inference in graphical models and supports probabilistic programming. It matters for .NET developers who want probabilistic models without leaving that ecosystem.

tiers.eli5: It's a toolkit for building models that reason about uncertainty, packaged for people who write .NET code.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to express models as graphical models and run Bayesian inference on them. The pitfall is that inference in complex models is approximate and can be slow or inaccurate depending on the model.
tiers.paperLevel: It provides Bayesian inference over graphical models and serves as a probabilistic programming platform, letting a model be specified declaratively and inference run over it. Accuracy and cost depend on the inference algorithm chosen for the model.

explainer.example: A developer could model a diagnostic problem as a graphical model in Infer.NET and query the posterior probability of a cause given observed symptoms.
